files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close — controller's checklist

Owner: D. Lindqvist. Complete in sequence; no skipping ahead.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, prepare one correcting journal entry per item.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 that pays in July. If such a period exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities; some months, every run pays in-month.
3. Confirm June prepaid amortization against the prepaid schedule, supporting contracts, and the GL. If it is missing, book June prepaid amortization as ONE combined journal entry—do not duplicate an existing posting. Apply the convention that a full month is taken in the month an item begins.
4. Book June depreciation per the fixed asset register, after confirming the entry is not already in the GL.
5. Compare June vendor-bill documents with the GL, verify expense coding, and reclass anything miscoded.
6. Prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis, after items 1-5 have been booked.
files.notes/company_background.md:
# Company background

Ashworth & Bell Advisors began in 2018 when former colleagues Mara Ashworth and Simon Bell started helping owner-led companies untangle operating problems that sat awkwardly between strategy, finance, and day-to-day execution. Their first engagements came through professional referrals: a planning workshop here, a process review there, followed by practical implementation support when clients needed more than a slide deck.

Today, the firm sells management advisory services, operating-model reviews, planning facilitation, performance reporting, and project-based support for growing businesses. Its clients tend to value plain language and usable recommendations. The team is small and deliberately mixed: analytical consultants work alongside strong project coordinators, while the founders remain close to client delivery. Internal discussions are candid, calendars are crowded, and draft documents often carry margin notes from several hands before reaching a client.

The company has matured without losing its workshop-like feel. Repeat clients provide a dependable base of work, supplemented by focused assignments and referral-led opportunities. The current priority is to sharpen how services are packaged, improve handoffs between sales and delivery, and make month-end administration less dependent on individual memory. Ashworth & Bell Advisors remains an ordinary going concern, balancing active client work with steady improvements to its own systems and market presence.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## Direction

Make Ashworth & Bell Advisors easier to understand at a glance: practical advisors who help leadership teams turn plans into operating routines. The tone should stay experienced, specific, and human—not glossy or overly corporate.

## Priorities

- Refresh the core brand language and service-page copy.
- Publish short, useful field notes drawn from recurring client questions.
- Run two webinars per quarter, with one focused on planning and one on execution.
- Test a partner co-marketing pilot with a complementary professional-services firm.
- Build a light referral follow-up rhythm for former clients and trusted introducers.

## Content themes

Focus on decision cadence, management reporting, role clarity, project recovery, and the practical mechanics of turning strategy into accountable work. Each topic should produce a primary article, a shorter email version, and several social posts.

## Delivery notes

Keep production manageable for the consulting team. Subject-matter experts may speak their ideas aloud; marketing can shape the first draft and return it for technical review. Webinars should favor a useful working session over a long presentation.

## Measures

Track qualified conversations, webinar attendance, partner-sourced introductions, repeat site visits, and newsletter replies. Review results quarterly and retire activities that create attention without credible client interest. Budget remains pending the Q2 close.
files.notes/prior_accountant_memo.md:
# Notes from the previous desk

D. Lindqvist—leaving the practical bits here because they are easy to miss:

- The bank usually posts its own fees and service charges near the end of the statement. We have historically booked those during close rather than during the month, so check the last statement days carefully.
- I was moving too quickly in June, and the expense coding on one or two vendor bills may be wrong. Treat the supporting documents in `bills/` as authoritative and reclass the GL where needed.
- The budget was fixed early in Q2. The one-off June projects were never included, and they should explain most of the large budget-to-actual variances.
- This month, the June 16-30 payroll run does not pay until the first days of July. The payroll register has the detail.
